text:
Sam: quick heads-up — I tried to split the tfstate for gpu-pools (moving cluster resources into terraform/gpu/state) and also renamed the state key. CI ran, rollback happened mid-move, now applies are failing with a stuck lock :grimacing:
Jin: ugh, what backend? S3/Dynamo or consul?
Sam: S3 backend + DynamoDB lock table. Error in GH Actions: ```
Error: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed

...
Lock Info:
  LockID: 7f9c2b0a-rename-split
  Holder: github-actions/pr-458
  Operation: state-move
  Who: sam@redwood
```
Marta: did the pipeline cancel during `terraform state mv`? That can leave the lock entry but the statefile partially moved.
Sam: yeah, workflow was cancelled by a force-push during the split. I see two state keys now: `global/terraform.tfstate` and `gpu/terraform.tfstate.partial-rename`
Oliver: partial keys are bad. If the lock references the new key but the object isn't fully written, a normal apply will hang because the backend thinks someone still owns it.
Jin: can you show the `dynamodb` row? sometimes TTL didn't propagate and lock stays until TTL expires.
Sam: dynamo row shows TTL = null, CreatedAt = 2026-03-18T10:12:33Z, and Info shows "operation: state-move"
Marta: If TTL missing, force-unlock might be necessary but risky. We should check whether that `github-actions/pr-458` runner is still alive and whether its temp creds rotated.
Sam: runner is gone. PR closed. No active processes.
tf-bot: deploy status: last run pr-458 -> cancelled, artifacts removed.
Jin: my vote: do a read-only inspect first. Run `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-terraform/global/terraform.tfstate` and `s3://redwood-terraform/gpu/` to see what objects exist. Also `aws dynamodb get-item --table-lock --key ...`
Sam: did that — global key exists and looks intact. gpu key is 128KB, but object content looks like a fractured state (two resource blocks concatenated, likely partial write).
Oliver: that explains the drift on imports. When we re-run, terraform compares state and sees duplicates -> tries to import or create -> gets blocked by the lock.
Marta: plan: (1) protect current real state (download both objects and store backups), (2) create a temporary workspace and manually reconcile the gpu state, (3) remove orphaned lock from Dynamo only after we are sure no runner is active. Whoever does force-unlock must attach the exact LockID to audit.
Sam: I'm in. I'll back up both files now and paste S3 object versions here.
Sam: backup done — uploaded to `s3://redwood-terraform-backups/tfstate/1844012345-global.tfstate` and `.../gpu.partial.1844012345.tfstate`
Jin: good. For the actual unlock, prefer `terraform force-unlock 7f9c2b0a-rename-split` from your laptop (not CI) so creds are traceable to your user. After unlock, re-run `terraform state pull` to confirm.
Marta: also check our GitOps Helm release for the gpu-operator — if Helm applied resources exist but terraform doesn't know about them we can end up with duplicate managing agents. We should annotate the helm release to pause automated rollouts during the reconciliation window.
Oliver: @Sam once you force-unlock, don't run the same state-move pipeline immediately. Instead, do a manual `terraform state list` in the tmp workspace and `terraform state mv` resource-by-resource, validating after each move. That avoids partial writes.
Sam: ok doing `terraform force-unlock 7f9c2b0a-rename-split` from my laptop now. Will post output shortly.
(oncall-bot): Reminder: any manual lock operations must be logged in #incidents if they touch production state.
Sam: force-unlock returned `Unlocked lock 7f9c2b0a-rename-split`
Jin: now pull both states and run `terraform state list` in the gpu file. Also check for duplicate resources like `module.gpu_pool.aws_instance.worker[0]` vs `module.cluster.aws_instance.gpu-worker-0`
Sam: found duplicates. I'm moving them one by one: `terraform state mv 'module.cluster.aws_instance.gpu-worker-0' 'module.gpu_pool.aws_instance.worker[0]'` -> success.
Marta: nice. After all moves, run `terraform plan -state=./merged.tfstate` to verify no adds/destroys.
Sam: plan shows 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. Good.
Oliver: re-upload merged state to `s3://redwood-terraform/gpu/terraform.tfstate` and then trigger a reconciled apply from CI but keep it in dry-run mode first.
Sam: uploaded new key and set a TTL on the dynamo lock table default. Also updated the pipeline to write a `state-move` marker file and to use multipart uploads with a final rename step so partial objects aren't visible to the backend during writes.
Jin: great. Can we also add a GitHub Actions job that sets a short Dynamo TTL (e.g., 60s) for state-move ops so a cancelled runner doesn't leave forever locks?
Marta: yes but we need to be careful — TTL too short and a long-safe operation could collide. Maybe 5 minutes with periodic heartbeat from the runner. If heartbeat stops, TTL expires and lock is auto-cleared.
Sam: adding follow-up ticket in eng-infra board: "state-move hardening: multipart + rename + lock heartbeats + documented force-unlock procedure". I'll paste the ticket link once created. :memo:
Jin: thanks for handling it cleanly. Two action items: update pipeline and document runbook for force-unlock + reconciliation.
Sam: noted. Closing thread once ticket created.
